method: GPT-6.1 matched the standard to BSmtLib's Lean without seeing the authors' citations: once from each of the 298 definitions, and once from each of the 352 rules and paragraphs of 2.7. It ran in a sandbox with no network.

A program scored its links against the citations in the authors' comments (106 definitions cite the standard), beside two controls: linking by name alone, and linking every passage to every definition.

From the standard: the authors' definition named

findings: BSmtLib names its definitions after the standard's rules, so matching by name alone finds 60 of the 81 rules.
GPT-6.1 found 73 of 81 from the code alone, and going from the standard to the Lean it named the authors' definition on 62 of 63 cited passages.
It explained 4 of the authors' 12 Readings from the code alone and 7 with comments kept, among them :56 (L5) and the missing define-funs-rec (L6).
We changed one detail in 12 definitions (a range, a release, an empty list). It caught all 12, naming an input each one treats differently, and called all 5 untouched ones exact.
The authors' paper says their formal reading was generated by AI and reviewed by the maintainer, so agreement here is not independent proof.
